recovered_memory.title: Unresolved is a valid continuity state
recovered_memory.summary: When source coverage is incomplete or candidate evidence fails provenance gates, continuity work must preserve the unresolved state rather than force coherence by reconstructing a plausible assignment. Resolution is an evidence transition, not a narrative obligation.

sources_inspected.observed_state: Production acceptance and deployment claims remain fail-closed when evidence is incomplete.

sources_inspected.privacy_treatment: Only the abstract operational principle is retained; no private text, speaker attribution, personal context, filename, or excerpt is copied into the repository.

sources_inspected.observed_state: Recent continuity commits preserve scope-bounded negative evidence, temporal precedence, fail-closed origin adjudication, and coordination-only trigger classification.

operational_rule.name: noncoercive_resolution

transition_conditions.unresolved_to_observed: An immutable source object explicitly establishes the claim within the eligible namespace and source class.
transition_conditions.unresolved_to_inferred: Multiple compatible sources support a bounded inference while the originating object remains absent; inference must not be labeled origin fact.
transition_conditions.unresolved_to_resolved: All required origin gates pass and coverage is sufficient for the asserted resolution class.
transition_conditions.remain_unresolved: Coverage is incomplete, any required gate fails or is unevaluated, or candidate evidence only improves plausibility without establishing identity.

operational_rule.prohibited_transition: No claim may move from unresolved to resolved solely because a coherent reconstruction can be narrated.

claims.text: The active queue requires unresolved retention and prohibits reconstruction of unverified M-series history.
Across operating rules and prior continuity adjudications, resolution functions as an evidence-qualified state transition rather than a requirement to eliminate contradiction.
All continuity schemas should reject unresolved-to-resolved transitions that lack an immutable source locator and passing required gates, even when a reconstruction is semantically persuasive.
A continuity gap should be filled with the most coherent reconstruction when exact history cannot be found.
The originating decision log, language lexicon, project document, or chat-history assignment for M-004, M-005, and M-006 remains unlocated.

contradiction_resolution.apparent_conflict: Continuity mining is tasked with resolving contradictions, while the evidence may not permit a definitive historical assignment.
contradiction_resolution.resolution: Resolve the contradiction at the rule level by distinguishing adjudication from closure: the team can determine that available evidence is insufficient and preserve that insufficiency as the accurate state.

next_resolution_step: Apply the noncoercive-resolution rule to every M-004/M-005/M-006 candidate during exhaustive branch and commit traversal; promote only candidates that pass the existing origin contract with immutable locators.
